name: Jack Grubman

summary.text: Jack Grubman was a telecommunications research analyst at Salomon Smith Barney, Citigroup's brokerage unit. On April 28, 2003, as part of the Global Research Analyst Settlement, the SEC, the New York Attorney General, the NASD and the NYSE announced that Grubman would be censured, permanently barred from the securities industry and pay $15 million, without admitting or denying the findings; half went to a distribution fund for Salomon Smith Barney customers and half was a penalty paid to New York.

facts.claim: On April 28, 2003 the SEC, the New York Attorney General, the NASD and the NYSE announced that Grubman would be censured, permanently barred from the securities industry and pay $15 million; he neither admitted nor denied the findings.

facts.claim: Half of Grubman's $15 million payment ($7.5 million) went to a distribution fund for Salomon Smith Barney customers and the other half was a penalty paid to the New York Attorney General; he may not seek reimbursement or indemnification for the amounts.

facts.claim: The SEC filed its federal court complaint against Grubman the same day, April 28, 2003, as part of the regulators' Global Research Analyst Settlement with ten firms.
